paper_metadata.title: Multicomponent Ni-rich high-entropy alloy toughened with irregular-shaped precipitates and serrated grain boundaries

evidence.quote: A novel precipitation-strengthened multicomponent Ni-rich Ni 46.23 Co 23 Cr 10 Fe 5 Al 8.5 Ti 4 W 2 Mo 1 C 0.15 B 0.1 Zr 0.02 (at.%) high-entropy alloy (HEA) was designed

we successfully developed a novel Ni 46.23 Co 23 Cr 10 Fe 5 Al 8.5 Ti 4 W 2 Mo 1 C 0.15 B 0.1 Zr 0.02 (at.%) MNi- HEA strengthened by coherent L1 2 precipitates using the computational-assisted CALPHAD method.

other.remelting: flipped and remelted at least four times

evidence.quote: alloy ingots were synthesized by arc-melting a mixture of pure metals (purity ≥ 99.95%) in a Ti-gettered high-purity argon atmosphere. The ingots were flipped and remelted at least four times
then drop-cast into a water-cooled copper mold to give flats with a dimension of 50 × 10 × 5 mm 3
The as-cast flats were firstly solution-annealed at 1200 °C for 2 h.
the STGBs were manipulated by oil-quenching (~250 °C/s) the solution-annealed flats down to room temperature followed by the same aging treatment (STG-MNiHEA)
followed by the same aging treatment (STG-MNiHEA). All aging treatments were finished by oil-quenching in the air atmosphere.

A novel precipitation-strengthened multicomponent Ni-rich Ni 46.23 Co 23 Cr 10 Fe 5 Al 8.5 Ti 4 W 2 Mo 1 C 0.15 B 0.1 Zr 0.02 (at.%) high-entropy alloy (HEA) was designed with strain-hardening after yielding rather than strain-softening even at the temperature of 10 0 0 °C.
Such an improvement of the strength and ductility has been attributed to the enhanced resistance of the serrated grain boundaries to the intergranular crack nucleation and propagation.
W and Mo were alloyed for solid-solution strengthening of the matrix and for slow coarsening kinetics of the precipitates
strains at the STGBs may probably be produced by slip-assisted grain-boundary sliding, and the accumulation of dislocations at the vicinity of grain boundaries
Such high strain localization suggests the STGBs with very limited capability to accommodate strains
Once the intergranular microcracks are initiated, they will expand readily and rapidly and therefore are easy to connect to form the straight intergranular crack path, leading to the fast fracture

The release of the intergranular strain localization via the SEGBs can be attributed to the limit of grain-boundary sliding, and the partition of strain into grain interiors instead of concentrating at grain boundaries

the SEGBs also suppress crack propagation because that the zigzag array of the initiated microcracks at the SEGB segments were diﬃcult to connect to form a serrated intergranular crack propagation path
The serrated-grain-boundaries (SEGBs) were introduced by furnace-quenching the solution-annealed flats down to 800 °C inside the furnace with a slow constant rate of ~0.17 °C/s
The irregular-shaped precipitates and SEGBs were introduced simultaneously in the SEG-MNiHEA by the furnace-quenching
the growth and coalescence of the particles during the oil-quenching were significantly suppressed for the relatively much faster cooling rate

The resultant HEA with irregular-shaped precipitates and serrated grain boundaries showed a brittle-to-ductile transition, giving in a superior strength up to as high as ~260 MPa while maintaining a uniform elongation of ~6.5%.
Such an improvement of the strength and ductility has been attributed to the enhanced resistance of the serrated grain boundaries to the intergranular crack nucleation and propagation.

Due to the rapid onset of intergranular cracking, the HEA with spherical precipitates and straight grain boundaries was brittle, exhibiting an inferior tensile strength of ~220 MPa, and an insuﬃcient uniform elongation of only ~1.9%.
A novel precipitation-strengthened multicomponent Ni-rich Ni 46.23 Co 23 Cr 10 Fe 5 Al 8.5 Ti 4 W 2 Mo 1 C 0.15 B 0.1 Zr 0.02 (at.%) high-entropy alloy (HEA) was designed
The serrated-grain-boundary architecture effectively overcomes this intergranular cracking issue.

Cracking along grain boundaries was found to be closely related to high strain localization, e.g., high strains at grain boundaries and very low strains within the grain interiors, as proved and unveiled by the EBSD KAM map
